title: Scaffold a FastAPI App
bottom_line: Type one command, answer a few questions, and Claude writes a FastAPI web app. Fill in `.env`, migrate, then run `make dev`.

sections.heading: One command starts a new web app

blocks.caption: Both flags are optional. Without them the app targets Railway and uses the AI model openai/gpt-4o-mini.

blocks.text: The skill scaffolds a complete FastAPI web application skeleton, drawn from production apps. **Scaffolding** means writing the starting files and folders of a new project, so you begin from a working app instead of an empty folder.

cards.title: Name the app
cards.text: `/fastapi-template:fastapi-template create a new app called my-app`

cards.title: Add flags
cards.text: `/fastapi-template:fastapi-template [--host railway|generic] [--ai-model <openrouter model id>]`. The defaults are railway and openai/gpt-4o-mini.

cards.title: Just describe it
cards.text: Say what you want in plain words, for example: "Scaffold a new FastAPI project for a task management app".

blocks.text: Claude also uses this skill on its own whenever you ask to create a new project, scaffold a web app, start a FastAPI app, set up a project skeleton, start a new web app, or bootstrap a Python web application from scratch.
The plugin needs no environment variables and has no plugin settings. The plan-tools plugin installs this plugin for you, and its create-webapp skill uses it to start a full app.

sections.heading: Two flags change where it deploys and which AI model it uses

rows: With `generic`, the skill leaves out the `Procfile`, the Railway deploy instructions and the ping retries for sleeping serverless containers.
The default model the app's AI helper (`invoke_ai_model`) sends requests to through OpenRouter.

blocks.text: With `--host generic` there is no Procfile and no Railway-specific code, so you deploy to any host that runs a Python web server. The app still reads `PORT` and its connection strings from the environment.

blocks.title: Opinionated defaults and how to change them
rows: Deploy to Railway: a `Procfile`, and database/Redis pings retried while a sleeping Railway service wakes up
AI calls go to OpenRouter with the model `openai/gpt-4o-mini`
Dev server on port 8000 in the main checkout, `8000+N` in each `claude --worktree` checkout
`PORT` in `.env`, the environment, or `make dev PORT=<port>`
Production server is gunicorn with 8 uvicorn workers
edit the `server` target in the generated `Makefile`
Database included; AI asked about; Redis included when AI is

sections.heading: Claude asks three questions before it writes anything

steps.title: The app name
steps.text: Claude asks for the app name in kebab-case (lowercase words joined by hyphens, like `my-app`) if you did not give one in the command.

steps.title: Which features to include
steps.text: Claude confirms which optional parts go in: the database, AI through OpenRouter, and Redis caching. The defaults are in the table below.

steps.title: Where to put it
steps.text: Claude asks for the target directory. The default is the current directory.

steps.title: Files are generated
steps.text: Claude then generates all the files of the project.

blocks.title: Optional features and their defaults
rows: yes if AI is included, otherwise ask

sections.heading: You get a full project folder with server, pages and database

blocks.title: The stack inside the generated app
rows: OpenRouter + Jinja2 prompt templates + Redis caching
Railway (Procfile) by default; with `--host generic`, no Procfile and no Railway-specific code

terms.definition: A Python framework for building web servers.
A small library that lets links and forms fetch new HTML from the server without reloading the page.
A small library for interface behaviour that stays in the browser, such as opening a menu.
The tool that applies database changes (migrations) in order.
A fast in-memory store, used here as a cache.
A service that forwards AI requests to many AI models through one API key.
A hosting service, the default place the app deploys to.
The tool that installs Python packages and runs the app.

blocks.title: What the generated app already does
items: Every link and form navigates without a full-page reload (hx-boost on the page body). This matters most when the app is wrapped with Capacitor, because a full-page reload flashes white and breaks the native app feel.
A failed request (server error, network/offline, timeout) shows the user visible feedback instead of leaving the page looking stuck.
Logins and other per-user state are kept in signed cookies, keyed by `SESSION_SECRET`.
Missing required environment variables make the app fail at startup, not on a request.
`DEV_MODE=ON` switches logging to DEBUG (INFO in production), turns off the secure flag on cookies, and adds `-dev` to the cache prefix.
Every request is logged with method, path, status and duration.
AI answers are cached in Redis.

sections.heading: Have these ready before you run the generated app

cards.title: uv and Python 3.11+
cards.text: `uv` and Python 3.11 or newer. The project pins 3.11 in `.python-version`.

cards.title: make
cards.text: For the `make dev`, `make server` and Alembic targets.

cards.title: PostgreSQL and Redis
cards.text: A PostgreSQL database and a Redis server, when those parts are included.

cards.title: OpenRouter API key
cards.text: Needed when the AI part is included.

cards.title: Railway account
cards.text: For deploying with the default host. The generated app has a `Procfile` that Railway runs.

sections.heading: Fill in .env, run the migration, then start the server

steps.title: Go into the project
steps.text: Open a terminal in the new folder.

steps.title: Create your .env file
steps.text: Copy the example settings file, then edit `.env` with real values (see the table below).

steps.title: Run the initial migration
steps.text: This runs the initial database migration.

steps.title: Start the dev server
steps.text: The app is now running at localhost:8000.

block.code: make dev              # start dev server at localhost:8000

blocks.title: Environment variables the generated app reads from .env
Quick Start in one block
blocks.code:
cd <app-name>
cp .env.example .env
# edit .env with real values
make alembic-upgrade  # run initial migration
make dev              # start dev server at localhost:8000

sections.heading: Each Claude worktree gets its own port, database and Redis

blocks.text: When you work in a `claude --worktree` checkout, a hook gives it its own `.env`: a port of `8000+N` (the main checkout stays on 8000), a Postgres database `<app_name>_wtN` with migrations applied, and Redis db `N`. Slots run from 1 to 9. So `make dev` can run in the main checkout and in every worktree at once.
Main's `ENGINE_URL` must point at a local/dev Postgres: worktree sessions create and drop `<app_name>_wtN` databases there.

rows: Set up this worktree by hand: write its `.env`, create its database and migrate it. Does nothing in the main checkout or if `.env` exists.
Drop the database and flush the Redis db of worktrees that no longer exist. The hooks also run this when a session starts or ends.

blocks.text: The main database and Redis db 0 are never touched.

sections.heading: Replace the example parts with your own

blocks.caption: After generating, Claude reminds you of these steps.

cards.title: Rename placeholders
cards.text: Replace all `<app-name>` placeholders with your actual app name.

cards.title: Fill in .env
cards.text: Put real values in `.env` (`ENGINE_URL`, `REDIS_CONNECTION_STRING`, and so on).

cards.title: Define your models
cards.text: Delete the example `Item` model in `db/models.py` and define your own.

cards.title: Write your prompts
cards.text: Replace the example `prompts/example.txt` with real prompt templates.

cards.title: Start the server
cards.text: Run `make dev` to start the dev server.

sections.heading: Example: a recipe app for any host with a different model

after.label: You get
after.text: A `recipe-box/` folder without a `Procfile`, with `invoke_ai_model` defaulting to that OpenRouter model.

blocks.code: /fastapi-template:fastapi-template create a new app called recipe-box --host generic --ai-model anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5
